pamphlet_excerpts: Question Art Occupied: The question of what “art” is has occupied the minds ofphilosophers and critics ever since humankind began to thinkand argue.
Term Applied Forms: The term has been applied to many forms of visualmedia, especially to the fine arts, drawing, painting, sculpture, and printmaking.
But Includes Architecture: But it also includes architecture, industrialdesign, fashion design, pottery, and weaving.
Differenceis Fine Arts: The differenceis that fine arts are concerned only with beauty and expressionand the others, though the art may be beautiful, focus firston function.
step_by_step_procedure: Concentrates Two-dimensional: This merit badge pamphlet concentrates on two-dimensional art, specifically drawing and painting in various media.
Requirement Introduces: One requirement introduces you to design applications in thefields of graphic arts and industrial design.
Learnabout Art History: After you learnabout art history and design principles, you will understandhow these fields relate to fine art.
Since Prehistoric People: Since prehistoric people first madecave paintings, artists have tried to portrayreality.

pamphlet_excerpts: Elements Art Design: Elements of Art and Design Balance Balance is the visual stability of the composition.
Workof Art Visual: If a workof art has visual balance, then the viewer feels that the elements have been arranged just right.
There Imbalance Then: If there is an imbalance, then the viewer feels something’s wrong, that the elementsneed to be rearranged.
Formal Balance Occurs: A formal balance occurs whensimilar elements are placed on eachside of the central axis (a drawn orimaginary line through the centerof the work).
step_by_step_procedure: Differentelements Art Line: The differentelements of art, line, value, shape, space, color, and texture, all influencethe visual weight of a composition.
Forexample Small Area: Forexample, a small area of bright colorcan balance a larger area of dull color.
Art Design Elements: Elements of Art and Design Elements of Artand Design When you create art, you are expressing your ideas, your feelings, or your beliefs.
Intend Share Art: If you intend to share your art with otherpeople, you need to know how to organize your design so thatthey will understand what your art is telling.

pamphlet_excerpts: Principles Guidelines: These principles are guidelines, notrules, to help you express yourself artistically.
Understandingthese Principles: Understandingthese principles also will help you to appreciate how other artists try to communicate through their work.
Six Principles Design: The six principles of design are rhythm, balance, proportion, variety, emphasis, and unity.
Rhythm Indicates Movement: Rhythm indicates movement by the repetition of a certain artelement or combination of elements.
step_by_step_procedure: Repeated Element Shape: The repeated element, a shape or line, for example, is called a motif.
Artistuses Repetition Motif: The artistuses the repetition of a motif to lead the viewer’s eye aroundthe work of art.
Random Rhythm Happenswhen: Random rhythm happenswhen a motif is repeated in noapparent order, with irregularspacing between one motifand the next.
Regular Rhythm Occurs: Regular rhythm occurs whenidentical motifs with identicalspacing between them arerepeated.

pamphlet_excerpts: Artists Line Color: Artists use line and color in different ways to make paintings.
Artwork Line Drawing: In some artwork, the line drawing is the basis for the paintingand color is a secondary element, added to describe the outlined forms.
Works Color Subject: In other works, color is the subject of the painting.
Matter Plan Color: No matter how you plan to use color, you need to knowhow to mix pigments and apply the paint.
step_by_step_procedure: Paint Formed Pigment: Paint is formed when a pigment is mixed with a bindingmedium.
Pigment Finely Ground: Pigment is finely ground, colored powder that comes from natural sources like minerals and plants or from chemicals.
Binding Medium Liquid: Binding medium is a liquid substance that holds pigment particles together and attaches them to a surface.
Substance Isalso Vehicle: This substance isalso called a vehicle because it “carries” the pigment.

pamphlet_excerpts: Artist Art Personal: An artist who makes art for personal pleasure does not have toget training.
But Want Career: But if you want a career in the visual arts, you willneed some formal lessons.
Colleges Universities Offer: Colleges and universities offer four- or five-year programsthat lead to the bachelor of fine arts and master of fine artsdegrees.
Programs Include Art: In addition to the core courses common to all majorareas of study, these programs include art history and studioart classes.
step_by_step_procedure: Portfolio Collection Samples: A portfolio is a collection of samples of the artist’sbest work.
Art Design Schools: Many art and design schools expect to see a portfolio and evaluate the student’s talent and qualityof work before they decide whether to accept him.
Year Various Schoolshost: Every year, various schoolshost a “portfolio day” so young artists can review their portfolios with representatives from many differentart.
Independent Schools Art: Independent schools of art and design offer two-year programs that lead to an associate of art or bachelor of fine artsdegree.
